# British Insurance Brokers’ Association (BIBA) – Written Evidence (CIM0007)

Summary

IInsurancebrokersareprimarilyagentsoftheclient.Theyhelpconsumersidentifysuitablecover,understand policy limitations, disclose relevant information, and access both standard and where needed, specialist markets where standard products may not meet their needs, they also represent clients during a claim, supporting them and representing them through the process. BIBA’s recommendations are focused on practical improvements that strengthen consumer understanding and reduce avoidable declined claims, without undermining the availability and affordability of cover.

iiHomeandtravelinsuranceprovideessentialfinancialresilienceformillionsofconsumers.Whenproductsare well understood and claims are handled well, insurance enables households and travellers to recover from events that would otherwise create serious financial hardship. # 1.Whatarethekeyareasofconcernforconsumersintheregulationofhomeandtravelinsurance

1In the main we believe consumer regulation for home and travel insurance by the FCAprovides some of the strongest customer protections in the world (we are members of the Worldwide Federation of Insurance Intermediaries). In fact, some of the processes to comply with FCAProduct ValueAssessment rules go far beyond other nations, are overly costly and require significant resourcein order to comply. There is an opportunitytorebalancethishighburdenofcompliancewhilemaintainingexistinghighlevelsofprotectionfor consumers. BIBAwelcome the Leeds reforms and subsequent Financial Services and Markes Bill and has a number of further proposals to reduce the frictional cost.

2Itisourunderstandingthatconsumersdonotthinkabouttheregulationofinsuranceproductsasamatterinits own right.At best, they may know that the industry will be regulated but may not even know who by and any question around regulation of the firms in the sector may only arise when consumers are unhappy about some matter connected to their specific cover.

3Consumers’focuswhenbuyinginsurancecouldbesummedupas‘affordability’,assincetheadventofdirect insurance offerings and price comparison websites, price sensitivity has become the main (and no doubt, in some cases, the only) consideration. The very name ‘price comparison site’rather than ‘product’or ‘policy’ comparison site clearly indicates this. People must not lose sight of the suitability of the product.

4Inpart,themisperceptionthatallcoveristhesame,playsintothefocusonpriceoverqualityofcover.The ongoing cost of living challenges may also be seen to exacerbate this.

5Industry participants havebecomeincreasinglyconcernedthatthefocus onobtainingthecheapestcover has created a protection gap, as underinsurance is a problem in both the consumer and small commercial insurance markets. There is clearly more work to do in filling not only the protection but also the knowledge gap for consumers, The consequences of always focusing on price may include consumers not receiving the ‘full’pay-out from their insurer that they were expecting, or worse, finding that they were not covered for the risk at all (a policy may be cheaper because it is a ‘stripped down’version to lower the price and so appear higher up the list of results on a comparison website). Brokers will ask a new customer what they are looking for from theirinsurance policy and do they have any unusual requirements orrisk exposures(for example,for travelinsurance–willtheybeengaginginanyunusualordangerouspursuits).Invariablytheanswerisprice, rather than cover.

6Travel insurance is a product where pre-existing medical conditions (PEMCs) play an increasingly significant part in the availability and pricing of the cover as medical costs can make up the largest proportion of a travel insurance claim. Claims for this can reach six figures as outlined in this [article](https://www.allcleartravel.co.uk/blog/real-cost-of-travel-insurance-claims/) from BIBAmember,AllClear. Thisismorelikelytohavetheattentionofconsumerswithmedicalconditions,ratherthanonhowthesectoris regulated.Primarilyincomplexmedicalhistoryscenarios,customersaretryingtoascertainiftheycanactually be covered. However, to achieve acceptance customers should definitely not be focused on achieving the lowest possible price. Instead, the focus should be on comprehensive cover if the worse should happen. This means making sure a customer declares all their medical conditions that fall within the medical warranty. If medical conditions are not fully disclosed, it is well within an insurer’s rights to refuse to pay a claim.

7The obligation on consumers to take reasonable care not to (deliberately or recklessly) misrepresent information is set out in the Consumer Insurance (Disclosure and Representations)Act 2012. The question becomes; how many consumers know this? Forms used in the application process will remind consumers about their obligations, but it is unclear as to what percentage of customers fail to make these disclosures (innocently or fraudulently) while considering the text of the policy. 22Pleaseseepoint35regardingembeddedinsurance.

23Regulatory disclosure requirements are also excessive meaning clients have to sift through far too much paperwork in long policy wordings and disclosure documents when they should be focusing on what is and is not covered. For example, ICOB 4.1.2 R (2) (requires an insurance intermediary to provide the customer with information on whether it has a direct or indirect holding representing 10% or more of the voting rights orcapital in a given insurance undertaking (that is not a pure reinsurer). 27As part of the transposition of the EU’s Insurance Distribution Directive in 2018, the FCAincorporated Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1469 of 11August 2017 laying down a standardised presentation format for the insurance product information document (known as an IPID) into its rules (as ICOBS 6Annex 3). The IPID design followed extensiveconsumertestinginfivecountriesbytheEuropeanInsuranceandOccupationalPensionsAuthority (EIOPA), including in the UK.

39Price comparison websites (PCWs) offer an accessible way for many consumers to purchase insurance (amongstotherproducts),andwerecognisethatconsumersarefreetochoosehowtheyobtaincover.Some ofBIBA’smembersmakeproductsavailableviathisdistributionchannel.Weunderstandthattheseplatforms have been working to improve how they present information and support customers.

# 5.Areconsumers’insuranceclaimshandledfairly?

52AccordingtotheFCA'sreviewintohomeandtravelclaimsin2025,therewereover2.5mhomeclaimsand over1.5mtravelclaimsbetween2022and2024,with73%and79%ofthoseclaimsacceptedrespectively. Over £9bn was paid to customers in response to those claims.

57If we draw on the experience of FCAsupervision of motor insurance claims, ( [https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/over-270000-motorists-receive-motor-insurance-compensation-](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/over-270000-motorists-receive-motor-insurance-compensation-) insurers); the FCAordered insurers to pay 270,000 motorists in the region of £200M, as the regulator consideredthatthesepolicyholdershadbeen'shortchanged'ontheclaimspaymenttheyreceivedaftertheir cars had been stolen or ‘written off’(considered uneconomical to repair). # c)Docashsettlementsdelivergoodoutcomesforconsumers?

61Cashsettlementsmaydeliveragoodoutcomefortheconsumerinsomecircumstances,forexample,wherea customer has already paid medical expenses themselves when attending a hospital abroad. In circumstances like this, a cash settlement may be exactly what the customer wants.

62It is not uncommon for insurers to make interim cash payments to customers, which may support customers’ ongoing or out-of-pocket costs while their claim is progressing.Amotorcyclist on holiday and involved in a trafficaccidentbutthankfullynotseriouslyharmedforexample,mayvalueaninterimcashpaymenttorecover the cost of a train ticket home, if their bike is too damaged to ride back.

63Inothercircumstances(suchascomplexclaims),acashsettlementwouldnotdeliverthebestoutcomeforthe customer, as the FCAreport pointed out. Claims that involve a need to rebuild or carry out extensive repairs like a flood loss to a home, would require professional claims support.Aflood claim will benefit from loss adjusters who can manage the process of making the property safe (e.g. damaged electrics, security risk or risk of damp). There will need to be an orderly process of drying out, disinfecting, redecorating, disposing of damaged materials safely and at the right time. It is difficult to predict the total likely cost and timeframe to put the customer back into the position they enjoyed before the event that led to their claim. This may mean the customer has to spend more time in alternative accommodation than originally assumed, which can be costly. Cash settlement in this scenario also puts the responsibility on the customer to project manage the work, hire tradespeople, etc., which they may not have the confidence or experience to do.

64Thecustomer’sindividualcircumstancesandtheparticularsituationgivingrisetoaclaimarelikelytodictate whether a cash settlement is in a customer’s best interests.
